about: Substrate lifecycle and the platform refresh reads; each route enforces its token organization/app grant.

decisions.demand: Substrate checks its sandbox app exists
decisions.why: a read scoped by the token's organization (404 for an app it cannot see)
an action: unique names, the token's organization
a computed read: the app's volumes (a deleted one pending_destroy until it is gone)
a create with the vendor's assigned fields
a move: pending_destroy (states.ts), then destroyed by the vendor

decisions.demand: Substrate lists running sandboxes; Runhuman 1 lists its workers
decisions.why: a computed read: the app's machines, destroyed ones left out

decisions.demand: Substrate launches a sandbox; Runhuman 1 a worker
decisions.why: an action: the machine made and launched (states.ts), its image run by the World's machine pool (ctx.machines); with a light pool, SDK command execution beyond node plus a folder-owned JS entry is unserved (shells, eval/flags, PTYs and other programs): the manifest's gap answers command admission before any machine state is created or process launched, as twin-world docs/contributing/architecture.md, Other wires: lanes, headers, line protocols, sockets and machines prescribes
a read, with the ports the pool published

decisions.demand: Substrate waits for started and stopped
decisions.why: a computed read: the state asked, or a timeout
a move started → stopped, the pool stops the image
a move stopped → started, the pool runs the image again

decisions.demand: Substrate stops a sandbox; Runhuman 1 destroys a worker
decisions.why: a move to destroyed (force), the pool removes the image
the held token organization and app caveats

decisions.demand: the World's own door, POST /_twin/tokens: { org, app? }: `fly tokens create org` (an organization token) or `fly tokens create deploy -a <app>` (a deploy token)
decisions.why: { org, app? }: `fly tokens create org` (an organization token) or `fly tokens create deploy -a <app>` (a deploy token), which no vendor API makes.

decisions.demand: the World's own door, POST /_twin/machines/{id}/exit: a machine's process exits on its own (a worker that drained its queue): stopped, and destroyed with auto_destroy
decisions.why: A machine's process exits on its own (a worker that drained its queue): stopped, and destroyed with auto_destroy, which no vendor API makes.
